clue.text: There's composure about Bill Walton's work

indicators.note: about here means one word is wrapped around the other, the second sitting inside

parts.note: to keep face is to keep one's composure, so face means composure
an ad, short for advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the calm that pervades a piece by the composer William Walton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' marks the container. Walton's Façade is a famous entertainment setting Edith Sitwell's poems to music.
explanation.definitionFit: Façade is the title of William Walton's celebrated entertainment for reciter and ensemble.

clue.text: Supporting firm about new time period

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: about says the firm word is placed around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: tight means firm or secure

explanation.surface: A firm backs a fresh period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside TIGHT, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortnight is a span of two weeks.

clue.text: Where you'd see main battleground

definitions.meaning: a main is a cockfighting match, staged in a pit for cocks
a ... is an arena of repeated conflict, as Belgium was called the ... of Europe

explanation.definitionFit: The pit for cockfights gives both the arena for a match and a figurative scene of many wars.

clue.text: Daughter's dark, small and neat

parts.note: inky means black as ink, dark

explanation.surface: A daughter is described as dark-haired, petite and tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinky is British informal for dainty, compact and neat.

clue.text: Scraping together a means to support Christian church

parts.note: a bra is a garment that supports the bust
Sion (Zion) is used for the Christian Church as the heavenly city of God

explanation.surface: Someone is gathering funds to keep a Christian church going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraping together' reads like raising money, but only 'Scraping' is the definition; 'together' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is the act of scraping or rubbing away a surface.

clue.text: Pause as a chapter's being rewritten

indicators.note: rewritten suggests the letters being put down again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, including the s
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A writer takes a break while a chapter is redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rewritten' signals the anagram, yet 'being' is also fodder: rearrange A CHAPTERS BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short rest or respite from activity.

clue.text: Snake overcoming vigilant guardian carrying a spear?

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming places the snake on top of what follows

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: carrying says the guardian holds the letter a inside it

parts.note: Argus was the hundred-eyed watchman of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A snake gets the better of a watchful sentinel armed with a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts A inside ARGUS. The question mark flags that 'spear' is a shoot of the vegetable, not a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is eaten as spears, the young edible shoots of the plant.

clue.text: President has imposed prohibition on a Japanese art form

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower
a ban is a prohibition
the letter a, with on placing the ban above it

explanation.surface: A head of state slaps a ban on an art form from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the traditional Japanese craft of flower arranging.

clue.text: Initialized names of the criminals here in the nick

indicators.note: Initialized means reduced to initials, so take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Criminals' names are logged here at the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like British slang for a police station, but it means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick.

clue.text: Publication that's in the pink

parts.note: a newspaper famously printed on salmon-pink paper, read as if it were in fine health

explanation.definitionFit: The London business daily is printed on distinctive pink newsprint.

clue.text: Dealing with abstruse ideas once tried out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of once tried are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has a go at abstruse ideas once, putting them to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONCE TRIED; the clue's letter count was lost from the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite describes learning that is obscure and handles little-known, difficult subjects.

clue.text: Field, in part, constituting fold

indicators.note: in places the field word inside the abbreviation for part

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word

explanation.surface: A field, partly, makes up a fold in the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' looks like 'partly', but 'part' is abbreviated and 'in' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a doubled-over crease pressed into fabric.

clue.text: Old waitress, quick on her feet

definitions.meaning: a waitress in a J. Lyons teashop, a British chain of the early twentieth century

explanation.definitionFit: Lyons teashop waitresses were nicknamed for their speed, and the adjective means brisk.

clue.text: What follows gathering at the farm

definitions.meaning: an outcome or consequence that comes after an event
a second crop of grass mown in the same season, math being an old word for mowing

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the consequences of an event and a farmer's second mowing of hay.

clue.text: If you want to eat nuts, you'll have to start quickly

definitions.text: If you want to eat nuts, you'll have to
definitions.meaning: literally, you must set about breaking the shells
an idiom meaning to begin promptly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to begin work at once, and literally describes breaking nutshells open.

clue.text: Course people follow

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
to track someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: People follow a set course.
explanation.definitionFit: A racetrack is a course laid out for racing.

clue.text: A record climb

parts.note: LP, a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record climbs the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, something one climbs.

clue.text: Part of saint's leg stiffening

parts.note: St Peter is the saint, so saint's gives Peter's
ham is the back of the thigh or a cured pig's leg

explanation.surface: A relic: part of a saint's leg has gone stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' reads as a link hinting that ham is part of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a stiff corded ribbon used to stiffen waistbands and hats.

clue.text: The end's in sight, I perceive

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words sight, I perceive

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that the finish line is at last visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks out the run straddling sighT I Perceive; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is the pointed end or extremity of something.

clue.text: Rider, very large man, mounted under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the reversed run below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the following run climbs upwards, read backwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
Ivor is a man's name, a crossword stock

explanation.surface: A rider, a huge fellow, gets on his horse while under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' reverses OSIVOR to ROVISO; 'under' sets it below P. 'Rider' is not a horseman but an added condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or qualification attached to an agreement, like a clause added on.

clue.text: Attack with rope produces criminal record

parts.note: to charge is to rush forward in attack
on a sailing boat a sheet is a rope controlling a sail

explanation.surface: Assaulting someone with a rope lands you with a police record.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheet is a sailor's rope, not bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge sheet is the police document listing accusations against a person in custody.

clue.text: Take advantage of daring deed

definitions.meaning: the verb sense, to use something or someone selfishly
the noun sense, a bold feat or adventure

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to make selfish use of; as a noun, a bold feat.

clue.text: Baseball player in trunks and jumper, for instance

parts.note: swimming trunks are a type of shorts
a jumper (a British word for a sweater) is an example of a top

explanation.surface: A ballplayer appears dressed in swimming trunks and a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop is the fielder positioned between second and third base.

clue.text: Belts — they're worn well below the waist

definitions.meaning: as a verb, belts means strikes or punches hard

definitions.text: they're worn well below the waist

explanation.definitionFit: To sock is to hit hard, and the hosiery is worn on the feet.

clue.text: Rag heard from Cockney musician

indicators.note: the word is said as a Londoner of the East End would say it, with the vowel shifted

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper or paper

explanation.surface: A ragtime tune is heard played by a musician from the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney (East London) speech the vowel of 'paper' is said like the one in 'pipe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is one who plays the bagpipes or pipe, a kind of instrumentalist.

clue.text: Flower-girl creates a moving image before end of play

indicators.note: before places the camera word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: to pan is to swing a camera across a scene, making a moving shot

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word play

explanation.surface: A flower girl films a sweeping shot just before the play ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The count is missing from the page. The answer is both a flower and a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The pansy is a garden flower, and the name was also given to girls.

clue.text: Greeting only half addressed to a friend

indicators.note: only half says just one of the two equal parts of the greeting is kept

parts.note: chin-chin is a toast or greeting said when drinking

explanation.surface: Someone offers a greeting to a pal, but only half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps one CHIN of CHINCHIN; 'addressed to' is a link. China means mate from rhyming slang 'china plate'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a china is a pal.

clue.text: Material churned up in stomach

indicators.note: churned up suggests the letters of in stomach being stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant is churning around in one's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Macintosh is a rubberised waterproof cloth, named after Charles Macintosh, its inventor.

clue.text: Most thickset un-English storekeeper

indicators.note: un-English tells us to drop the letter standing for English

parts.note: stockiest means most thickset or sturdily built

explanation.surface: A burly shopkeeper is said to be not English at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockist is a shop or trader that keeps particular goods in stock for sale.

clue.text: Political order making extremes of stupidity stop

indicators.note: extremes of says to take the first and last letters of the word stupidity

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it

explanation.surface: A political regime is ending acts of extreme stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised scheme of government or social arrangement.
